_about: Thursday: Ask Intimova (carousel, 5–6 slides on cream). One question people are too shy to ask out loud, answered warmly and plainly. Slide 1 is the question in their words; the middle slides are the answer; the last slide is the takeaway and 'Full answer: link in bio' (the article URL goes in the Facebook caption). Never say a follower sent the question: it's 'the question people are too shy to ask', not a made-up DM. The answer comes ONLY from the item's intimova.ng article (state/site/article-<slug>.txt in cloud runs), in its meaning and, where quoted, its words; 'says' holds sentences checked on the article on 30 Oct 2026. No anatomical words on slides, never a price from an article (prices come from npm run products). Space at least 6 weeks from a Monday myth or Tuesday carousel on the same article or topic (see 'space_from'). status: ready, hold (Grade decides) or used.

items.question: Is it normal that I don't finish from sex alone?
says: Is it normal to not orgasm from penetration alone? Yes — it’s the experience of most women, not a minority.
It reflects anatomy, not a flaw in you or your relationship.
items.angle: Yes, and you're in the majority. It's how bodies are built, not a flaw in you or him. What helps: knowing what you like, and saying it.

items.question: If I bring a toy into the bedroom, will my partner feel replaced?
says: A toy adds sensation and play to what you already share; it doesn’t replace anyone.
Couples who use toys together often report feeling closer, because the conversation itself builds trust.
items.angle: Name the real worry ('am I not enough?') out loud. A toy adds to what you share; it doesn't replace anyone.

items.question: Will the delivery rider know what's inside?
says: Your order ships in a plain, unbranded parcel — no product pictures, no store name, no description of the contents anywhere on the outside.
The rider is delivering a sealed box like any other — they don’t know, and have no reason to ask, what’s inside.
items.angle: No. A plain, unbranded box, handed over to a name. It looks like any other parcel.

items.question: What will show up on my bank statement?
says: At Intimova, privacy is built into every order: plain packaging, name-only delivery, neutral payment, and a private WhatsApp channel from first question to final handover.
items.angle: Privacy doesn't stop at the box: neutral payment, and one private WhatsApp chat from question to delivery.
items.notes: Say only 'neutral payment', as the article does. Don't name the exact descriptor text: the article doesn't give it.

items.question: Why don't I feel like it anymore?
says: Notice how little of that is about being "broken". Most of it is biology and circumstance doing exactly what biology and circumstance do.
If low desire is sudden, persistent, distressing, or clearly tied to a new medication, it’s worth a conversation with a doctor
items.angle: Stress, sleep, hormones, medication and time all move desire around. For many people desire shows up after closeness begins, not before. When to see a doctor.

items.question: Why do I finish so fast?
says: Finishing sooner than you’d like is extremely common, especially when you’re anxious, over-excited or out of practice.
If it’s new, persistent and genuinely distressing, or comes with other symptoms, see a doctor — the cause is often straightforward.
items.angle: Nerves and pressure are the usual causes, not a flaw. It's a skill you can build. When to see a doctor.
items.notes: Don't repeat the article's 'rarely a medical problem' on a slide; the library's sourced wording is in althof-2014-pe and cooper-2015-pe-techniques.

items.question: If I'm dry, does it mean I'm not attracted to him?
says: Being dry doesn’t mean you’re not attracted to your partner or that something’s wrong — it’s ordinary variation.
items.angle: No. Cycle, stress, sleep, some medicines and life stage all change it. Give it time, use a good water-based lube, and see a doctor if it hurts.
items.notes: Don't use the article's title wording on slides.

items.question: I've never bought a toy. Where do I even start?
says: The short version: start small, quiet and body-safe, and don’t overthink the first one. You’re not making a lifetime commitment — you’re learning what you enjoy.
items.angle: Small, quiet, body-safe. It's not a lifetime commitment; you're learning what you enjoy.

items.question: How do I clean my toy, and where do I keep it?
says: Rinse it with warm water and a mild, fragrance-free toy cleaner after each use, dry it, and store it somewhere clean and private.
items.angle: Rinse, dry, store somewhere clean and private. Body-safe silicone is easy to keep hygienic.

items.question: We've been together for years and it feels like routine. Is that bad?
says: If sex has slipped into the same reliable routine, that’s normal — and completely fixable.
The golden rule: novelty plus communication .
items.angle: Normal, and fixable: something new, and talking about it. Change the room, the time, who leads.
items.notes: Suggestive only: skip the article's explicit ideas.

items.question: How do I bring up trying something new without it sounding like a complaint?
says: Raise it in a relaxed, clothed moment as something you’re curious about together — not a complaint.
items.angle: Pick a relaxed moment, not mid-moment. Make it 'we're curious', not 'you're lacking'.
items.notes: Never a price from this article (it says 'around ₦14,000' for the Bullet; the live price differs).
